samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because

Floating-point addition is not associative because the finite precision of the mantissa forces intermediate results to be rounded to the nearest representable value. This rounding error depends on the relative magnitudes of the operands, so adding a very small number to a large one can completely lose the small number's contribution. Consequently, grouping operations differently—such as (a + b) + c versus a + (b + c)—yields different intermediate rounded values, leading to different final sums.

Floating-point numbers have finite precision, so every arithmetic operation's exact result is rounded to the nearest representable value.
